answer: On an epoch boundary, agents must deposit a thread of proof-by-repeated-locked-step compute. Each thread’s tail merges into a pearl of hard-coded puzzle samples, burned at 60-bit depth. To Sybil, the attacker must repartition the thread end-to-end per head—each fake must regenerate 1.28ms of pearl-resistance. The pearl’s fixed-resolution cost blocks parallel execution; sequential embedding limits boosts to 0.7 scale. Ember checks verify thread and pearl joint consistency, dropping forks that diverge faster than target depth.
